The book's core identification of grapes as the yielded persons of a nation (works ripened into people, God seeking judgment/righteousness from them) is a precise extension of the consensus fruitfulness/v vineyard-yield motif. It retains the central referent (grapes = covenant fruit/righteousness) but narrows the referent to the people themselves as the yield, rather than their works or character. This is a boundary refinement, not replacement.

The book adds the explicit equation of grapes with 1) the people found by God (good man = missing cluster, remnant = blessing) and 2 the pressed grape yielding blood of covenant or wrath. It excludes the consensus's separate 'abundance of the land' and 'joy' strands while retaining judgment and Eucharistic blood motifs. The sour/wild grapes for unfaithfulness remain, but now directly tied to the people as grapes.

The printed citations provide strong support for the book's synthesis. 

Final classification: REFINED. 

This classification treats the book's emphasis on grapes as the people themselves as a narrowing of the consensus fruitfulness motif, while preserving its core themes of righteousness, judgment, and covenant blood. The extension shows the book focuses more tightly on the people as yield and the remnant motif, excluding broader land-blessing or joy interpretations. The citations strongly back the book's references to Isaiah 5, Hosea 9, Micah 7, Isaiah 65, Genesis 49, and Revelation 14. 

This is a coherent refinement rather than a full replacement or contradiction. {
  "relation": "REFINED",
  "consensus_summary": "Grapes primarily symbolize spiritual fruitfulness/righteousness expected from God's people as the vine/vineyard (good grapes for faithfulness, wild/sour for unfaithfulness/apostasy), with common secondary senses of land-abundance/blessing, divine judgment (ripe grapes crushed in the winepress of wrath), and Eucharistic blood of Christ via the fruit of the vine/wine.",
  "book_summary": "Grapes are a nation's works ripened into its people—persons as the vineyard's yield; God looked for grapes of judgment and righteousness and found men (Israel like grapes in the wilderness, the good man the missing cluster, the remnant the blessing left in it); pressed, the grape yields blood as the cup of the covenant or the cup of wrath according as the vintage is grapes or wild grapes.",
  "consensus_core_identification": "the (good or wild) fruit of the vine/vineyard = spiritual fruitfulness/righteousness or its lack (plus wine-source for blessing, Eucharist, or wrath)",
  "book_core_identification": "persons/people themselves as the vineyard's yield (ripened national works), good or wild, that when pressed give covenant or wrath blood",
  "core_relation": "BOOK_NARROWS",
  "extension_relation": "PARTIAL_RECLASSIFICATION",
  "boundary_disagreement": "Consensus treats vineyard/people and grapes/fruit as distinct (grapes = deeds or land-produce) and freely admits pure material abundance (Eshcol), joy, or the sour-grapes proverb; book collapses the yield into the persons/men themselves and centers only the people-quality + pressed-blood axis.",
  "material_contradiction": "None; people-as-fruit is already present by metonymy or simile in consensus-cited texts (Mic 7, Hos 9, Isa 65, Rev 14) and is compatible with fruitfulness/judgment/Eucharistic readings.",
  "rationale": "Minimum cores overlap on the shared multivalent cluster (good/wild quality tied to righteousness, remnant, and pressed blood for covenant or wrath) drawn from the same texts; the book preserves that category but materially narrows and re-precisionizes the referent to 'persons as the vineyard's yield' (works ripened into people), reclassifying cases that consensus leaves as abstract fruit, land-blessing, or vine-versus-fruit distinction. This is boundary refinement, not replacement of the central symbolic frame or a novel invention.",

  "confidence": "high"
}
